text:
sqlpipe moves data from Postgres to S3 in three stages.

The reader process connects to Postgres and streams rows in batches. It reads a fixed number of rows at a time, so memory use stays flat for a large table.

The converter takes each batch and builds a Parquet row group. Parquet is a column format that stores values by column, not by row. Each row group holds the converted rows and its own column statistics.

The uploader writes the Parquet output to S3 as a multipart object. A multipart object is one file that S3 receives in separate parts. If a part fails, the uploader retries that part with backoff. Backoff means the wait time grows after each failed try.

The three stages run as a pipeline. The reader fills batches while the converter and the uploader work, so no stage waits for the whole table.
